correctness.rationale: PASS: For each exactly specified n=2^k with 1<=k<=10 the complete finite set of n*n (start,length) cyclic substrings is grouped by literal equality; all resulting coverage masks are exact. The recorded upper set intersects every mask. The 1-to-21 selected factor weights are nonnegative exact integers over denominators at most eight, with per-coordinate sum at most the denominator. Summing these dual constraints bounds every attractor below by the weighted total; the ceiling equals the explicit upper size in all ten cases (including 51/8 rounding to seven at n1024). Sorting distinct masks by cardinality and deleting masks with a contained predecessor computes all inclusion-minimal masks; their irredundancy follows by taking each mask complement. A standard-library checker reconstructs every input word and all masks directly from the embedded package, checks all inequalities, factor counts, antichain counts, and succeeds. No infinite extrapolation is claimed.

value.rationale: PASS: Natural dyadic scales of a canonical 2-automatic word form a motivated finite classification, including the first of the examined dyadic lengths requiring seven circular-attractor positions. Beyond numerical optima, the complete irredundant circular coverage hypergraph is enumerated at all ten scales; at n1024 it has 55 essential masks for 868847 distinct circular factors, and 21 rationally weighted factors provide a compact sharp lower certificate. These masks characterize every circular attractor regardless of cardinality and are not available from the pre-existing ordinary-factor data. The proof does not assert all-length behavior or all optimal-set counts.
